presentation.label: TAPE SATURATION
presentation.summary: JClones TapeHead on the DSP: a small tape-style saturator with drive, trim and three tone colours.
presentation.overview: TapeHead runs the input through a two-state recursion whose corner frequency COLOR sets, drives both states into cubic smoothstep curves and adds a clipped feedback term. Low DRIVE gives gentle rounding and a slight tilt; high DRIVE flattens peaks and thickens the low end. It is a buffer-free insert, so it runs on FX1 or FX2 of every track.
highlights: Port of JClones_TapeHead.jsfx, within 4.7e-4 of the float reference in a native render
DRIVE and TRIM as continuous 0-127 knobs over the JSFX ranges
COLOR: NORM, MED and BRGT corners at 2100, 3680 and 5000 Hz
No buffers: FX1 or FX2 on any track, 288 cycles/sample static
usage: Assign TAPEHEAD in FUNC + FX2 (or FX1) SETUP with LEVEL and YES. Defaults match the JSFX: DRIVE 36, TRIM 18 (-3 dB), COLOR NORM.
Raise DRIVE for more saturation; lower TRIM (towards 0) to bring the level back up, raise it to attenuate down to -21 dB.
Use COLOR for brightness: MED and BRGT move the recursion's corner up and let more top end through the saturator.

controls.name: DRIVE
controls.doc: Tape drive. 0-127 maps to the JSFX drive 1-10 (gain 0.8x to 8x into the curves); 36 is about the JSFX default 3.5.

controls.name: TRIM
controls.doc: Output trim. 0 is 0 dB, 127 is -21 dB; 18 is the JSFX default -3 dB. Higher values are quieter.

controls.name: COLOR
controls.doc: Corner frequency of the recursion: NORM 2100 Hz, MED 3680 Hz, BRGT 5000 Hz.

limitations: The JSFX Clip switch is not exposed. Clip is always on (the JSFX default), because Q1.23 cannot carry the unclipped mode.
Corner frequencies assume 44.1 kHz, the rate every Octamod effect assumes.

presentation.overview: Choose FM SYNTH alongside FLEX and STATIC. controls.name: PTCH
controls.doc: SRC A: raw 64 is 0 semitones; raw 0–127 gives −64…+63. Scale and chromatic edits can constrain pitch.

controls.name: RATO
controls.doc: SRC B: raw>>2 selects 32 modulation ratios from 0.25 to 16; default raw 12 gives ratio 1.

controls.name: INDX
controls.doc: SRC C: FM modulation depth, raw 0–127. Zero produces the unmodulated carrier.

controls.name: FINE
controls.doc: SRC D: raw 64 is 0 cents; raw 0–127 gives −64…+63 cents.

controls.name: FDBK
controls.doc: SRC E: modulation-operator feedback, raw 0–127. Extreme feedback can be bright and alias.

controls.name: DEC
controls.doc: SRC F: modulation-index decay. Default raw 40 displays about 199 ms. This is separate from the AMP gain envelope.

controls.name: VOIC
controls.doc: LFO C: effective voice count 1–4. Values outside 1–4, including raw 0, normalize to one voice. Initial inherited LFO value displays one; four voices share the track filter and AMP.

controls.name: CHRD
controls.doc: LFO F: 32 chord shapes with four inversions each, encoded as shape<<2 | inversion. ---- uses individual played/recorded notes.

controls.name: LEG
controls.doc: FUNC+AMP F: OFF retriggers, MONO preserves one envelope across overlapping keys, POLY enables paraphonic legato. Ordinary sample tracks expose OFF/MONO.

controls.name: SCALE
controls.doc: OFF restores stock pitch behavior; select a scale to constrain PTCH edits, locks and chromatic keys.

controls.name: ROOT
controls.doc: Root of the scale and chromatic keyboard. Ignored with SCALE OFF.

controls.name: GLIDE
controls.doc: OFF or 1–127 slide time; the track LEG setting controls legato.

limitations: Parts store stock FLEX kind 1 plus FM/1 in unused NEIGHBOR control bytes. A stock build reads the track as FLEX; it does not synthesize FM. Choose stock explicitly before downgrading.
LFO3 speed/depth become VOIC/CHRD; LFO3 depth is muted. ATK/HOLD/REL remain inherited stock AMP controls and drive the synth’s own envelope.
The matching quantizer is bundled privately because the engine shares its mailbox and fixed scale accessor. Do not also select the public Scale Quantizer.

Cannot combine with Analog BD or the public Scale Quantizer because their native hooks overlap. Compatible mixed builds have native/browser byte-parity evidence; mixed audio loads have not been stress-tested.
Saved project/Part reloads, MIDI, chords, legato, modulation, maximum simultaneous voices and hardware timing remain unqualified.
Historical upstream marker-FLEX activation remains for compatibility; the verified route is the dedicated FM SYNTH chooser.

presentation.label: TRACK-KEYED COMPRESSION
presentation.summary: Drive the stock COMPRESSOR detector from any audio track, with key filtering, gain and audition controls.
presentation.overview: The stock COMPRESSOR gains KEY, KFLT, KGN and MON beside RMS on its SETUP page. Choose T1-T8 as the detector input, filter and adjust the key, or audition it on the receiving track.
highlights: KEY selects OFF or any of T1-T8, including the other DSP core.
KFLT provides low-pass, bypass and high-pass key filtering.
KGN applies a smoothed, stepped detector gain; 64 is unity.
MON auditions the processed key on the receiving track.
Stock ATK, REL, THRS, RAT, GAIN, MIX and RMS remain available.
usage: Select COMPRESSOR in FUNC + FX1/FX2 SETUP with LEVEL and YES.
Hold FUNC and press the selected FX button to open SETUP; choose the key with encoder C.
Turn MON off before normal listening; KEY OFF restores self-keying.

controls.name: ATK
controls.doc: Stock attack control, raw 0-127; determines how quickly compression engages. Exact time mapping is inherited from stock.

controls.name: REL
controls.doc: Stock release control, raw 0-127; determines recovery after detector level falls.

controls.name: THRS
controls.doc: Stock threshold, raw 0-127; lower it until the selected key causes gain reduction.

controls.name: RAT
controls.doc: Stock compression ratio, raw 0-127; raise it to increase compression.

controls.name: GAIN
controls.doc: Stock output make-up gain, raw 0-127. This is distinct from KGN, which changes the detector input.

controls.name: MIX
controls.doc: Stock dry/wet balance, raw 0-127; 127 is fully processed and 0 is dry.

controls.name: RMS
controls.doc: Stock RMS detector control, raw 0-127; retained on page 2 without changing its implementation.

controls.name: KEY
controls.doc: OFF restores self-keyed stock detection; 1-8 selects absolute T1-T8, including tracks on the other DSP core.

controls.name: KFLT
controls.doc: 0-63 low-pass; 64 bypass; 65-127 high-pass. LCD shows LP/OFF/HP. One-pole filter uses a 32-entry 40-2200 Hz table and special near-bypass edges; no exact cutoff readout.

controls.name: KGN
controls.doc: Raw 0-127 about unity at 64. Sixteen 8-value buckets yield -24 to +21 dB in 3 dB steps; the gain is smoothed with a nominal 5 ms block-rate time constant. LCD displays the stock bipolar raw offset, not dB.

controls.name: MON
controls.doc: OFF is normal compression; ON plays the processed key on this receiving track instead of its output, after both effects. MON requires a selected KEY.

limitations: Replaces COMPRESSOR on FX1 and in the FX2 chooser with the same stock effect ID 0x18; the visible effect name remains COMPRESSOR.

With Keep stock FX2 effects on, SPRING REV gives up its code space for this module; reassign any old SPRING REV slots. With it off, every stock FX2 effect leaves the FX2 chooser and the stock FX1 effects stay.

It builds beside the other Modwerk modules unless native octabam and Modwerk both refuse the selection. Among the nine visible modules other than Analog BD it builds beside every other module and every pair, and 798 of the 882 selections that build without it still build with it; the other 84, which hold Euclid or Scale Quantizer with at least two more modules, run out of effect-menu space. The selection checker says which applies.
It cannot be combined with Analog BD, which currently runs with the original effects only, or with MIDI Scenes, which is standalone firmware.
Its core-private keybus and cross-core window overlap BusDelay and BusVerb, which Modwerk does not carry; the native resource ledger refuses them beside it.
MUTE_MODES is not imported here. The author reports that muted-key behavior with MUTE_MODES needs its matching integration variant.
Cross-core keys use a buffered shared window. Core rate-locking and real-time race behavior require hardware qualification; no exact hardware latency is claimed.
The fixed-key MON stash is indexed by the source track. Simultaneous compressors sharing one KEY with different key processing need explicit interaction testing.
Every download carries the core logger; the module's LCD pages are identical with and without it.
No current Modwerk hardware, audio or maximum-load result is claimed. Emulator captures show the UI only, from an MKII panel, and do not qualify audio, transport or MKI operation.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial: duck T5 from a T1 kick
steps: Back up the project, work on a disposable copy, and put a kick on T1 and a sustained sample or loop on T5. Build with Modwerk; with Keep stock FX2 effects on, SPRING REV gives up its code space, so reassign any track that used it.
Select T5, hold FUNC and press FX1, turn LEVEL to COMPRESSOR and press YES. Press FX1 for the main page; hold FUNC and press FX1 to return to SETUP with the key controls.

Set KEY to T1, KFLT to 64, KGN to 64 and MON to OFF. On the main page, keep MIX at 127, raise RAT and lower THRS until the T5 signal dips when the T1 kick plays; adjust ATK and REL for the desired envelope.
Briefly set MON to ON on page 2 to hear the processed T1 key on T5, then return MON to OFF. Try KFLT below 64 to focus on bass, or above 64 to remove bass from the detector.
Return KEY to OFF and MON to OFF to restore self-keyed stock compression. Set MIX to 0 for the dry signal or select NONE to remove this effect; stop transport before saving the disposable project.
